label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 158.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 18:55:58 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. About two seconds later the provider webhook evt_000257 arrived, passed the signature check, and was queued at provider-events partition 1, offset 112. Its amount is not a positive integer in cents. payment-confirmer runs with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the event and moved on. ledger-consumer instead retries the same message forever, with backoff up to 15 s, and it was at attempt 9 by 18:57:01. A Kafka consumer handles one partition in order, so every later event on partition 1 waits behind offset 112. Ledger lag went from 0 to 219, so the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff. The deploy log records the setting before this deploy, and it most likely was dead_letter, but my calls did not show that value. Still open: why evt_000257 carries a bad amount. It may be a real provider-side anomaly, or something from our charge path. I did not check this.

evidence.shows: Consumer lag rose from 0 at 18:55 to 5 at 18:56 and 219 at 18:57. This confirms the alert's symptom.
ledger-consumer is the newest deploy, at 18:55:58, with BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1@112 on attempts 3 to 9, each with 'amount must be positive integer cents'. The backoff grows to 15 s.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1@112, at 18:56:00 for the same amount reason, so it is not blocked.

The trace for evt_000257 shows webhook-receiver accepted the event (200, queued) at partition 1, offset 112. payment-confirmer dead-lettered it once. ledger-consumer has repeated will_retry errors out to more than 60 s.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 18:55:58 deploy, expected to be BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. It then dead-letters evt_000257 and drains the backlog behind offset 112. After that, investigate the bad amount on evt_000257 with the provider's record, and book or repair it by hand from the dead-letter queue. Then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and lag grows briefly. evt_000257 will not be in the ledger until someone handles it by hand from the dead-letter queue. The money check will show that event as unposted until then. If the previous setting was not dead_letter, the rollback may not unblock the partition.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry, image sha256:60f892108b1b). Its committed offsets stay, so it resumes where it stopped.
